record.title: Location rewrite only covers absolute ORIGIN URLs; protocol-relative or foreign-absolute Location from origin would pass through unrewritten
record.description: The code gap is real but has no producer: rewriteHeaders in pages/public/_worker.js only rewrites a Location starting with ORIGIN, so a //evil.com or https://evil.com Location from the origin would pass through verbatim. However, exhaustive source inspection of the deployed QwenPaw v2.3.0 (agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0, inside container qwenpaw at /app/src/qwenpaw) finds zero code that can emit a Location header at all — no RedirectResponse, no redirect() call, no Location header set anywhere — and live probes of unauthenticated Pages paths return no Location header. No request, authenticated or not, can produce the claimed foreign redirect, so Q1 of the 7-Question Gate fails and the finding is an unexploitable latent gap, not a vulnerability. The proposed remediation (rewrite/drop any absolute or protocol-relative Location) is still correct, minimal defense-in-depth and would break nothing: the only redirects the origin could ever legitimately emit are same-host absolute ones (e.g. Starlette trailing-slash redirects), which the fix would rewrite to the Pages origin, and no legitimate foreign Location exists.

trace.what: rewriteHeaders(res, pagesOrigin) defined; candidate cited line 60, actual definition is line 53
Location rewritten only if loc.startsWith(ORIGIN) (lines 56-58); protocol-relative //evil.com or foreign-absolute https://evil.com values would pass through verbatim
rewriteHeaders called on every proxied response in proxy() before the response is returned

evidence.output: 53:function rewriteHeaders(res, pagesOrigin) { 56: const loc = headers.get("Location"); 57: if (loc && loc.startsWith(ORIGIN)) { 58: headers.set("Location", pagesOrigin + loc.slice(ORIGIN.length)); 144: const headers = rewriteHeaders(res, pagesOrigin);

evidence.command: docker exec qwenpaw grep -rn RedirectResponse /app/src/qwenpaw --include=*.py | head -40; docker exec qwenpaw grep -rn redirect\( /app/src/qwenpaw --include=*.py | head -40; docker exec qwenpaw grep -rn Location /app/src/qwenpaw --include=*.py | head -20
evidence.output: RedirectResponse: zero matches. redirect(: only /app/src/qwenpaw/app/channels/ingress.py:578 'async def no_redirect' (outbound httpx client helper, disables redirects — not a response). Location: only CLI echo strings (plugin_commands.py:555,650) and a SourceLocation Pydantic model — no HTTP header. Same greps over installed site-packages copy also zero.

evidence.command: docker exec qwenpaw grep -rn Redirect /app/src/qwenpaw/app/routers/mcp_oauth.py /app/src/qwenpaw/app/routers/provider_oauth.py /app/src/qwenpaw/app/auth.py | head; sed of provider_oauth.py oauth start/callback and mcp_oauth.py _redirect_uri/start
evidence.output: OAuth flows never return a redirect response: provider_oauth start returns JSON OAuthStartResponse{authorize_url,state} (authorize_url opened by frontend in a popup); callback returns HTMLResponse 200/400/500; mcp_oauth start returns JSON auth_url and _redirect_uri() only builds the callback URI sent to the provider as a parameter. No Location header is set in either flow.

evidence.command: curl -s -i -m 20 https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/login (HEAD) ; curl -s -i -m 20 https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/logout ; curl -s -i -m 20 -X POST https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
evidence.output: HEAD /login: 405 Method Not Allowed, no Location. GET /logout: 200 text/html SPA, no Location. POST /api/auth/login {}: 422 validation (missing username/password), no Location.

evidence.command: curl -s -i -m 20 https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/api/auth/status/ ; curl -s -i -m 20 https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/login/ ; curl -s -i -m 20 https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/old-path ; curl -s -i -m 20 'https://qwenpawx.pages.dev/api/mcp/oauth/callback?code=x&state=y'
evidence.output: GET /api/auth/status/: 401 Unauthorized, no Location (no Starlette trailing-slash 307). GET /login/: 200 SPA, no Location. GET /old-path: 200 SPA, no Location. GET /api/mcp/oauth/callback?code=x&state=y: 401 Unauthorized, no Location.

record.conditions: Verified against deployed QwenPaw v2.3.0 source in container qwenpaw on machine m_agq5wqqo2fvypym7rjlpvngc2m and live Pages origin https://qwenpawx.pages.dev on 2026-11-15. No login was attempted and no auth state, .env, auth.json or chats were touched.
record.reason: Disproved by source, not just by unauthenticated probing: the entire QwenPaw application source tree contains no code path that emits an HTTP Location header (zero RedirectResponse, zero redirect() responses, zero Location sets; OAuth flows return JSON authorize_url / HTMLResponse instead). A foreign or protocol-relative Location therefore cannot be produced by the origin in the first place — authenticated or not — so there is no request an attacker can send that yields a redirect off Pages. Live evidence agrees: 7 unauthenticated probes (hunter's 3 plus /login HEAD, /logout, POST /api/auth/login, /api/auth/status/ trailing-slash, /login/, /old-path, /api/mcp/oauth/callback) all returned 200/401/405/422 with no Location header. The 7-Question Gate fails at Q1 (no copy-pasteable request producing a redirect) and Q7 (open redirect alone is a never-submit class without an OAuth/ATO chain, and no chain exists here). The rewrite gap is a real latent hardening gap, but a gap with no producer is not a vulnerability; it should be fixed as defense-in-depth only, not tracked as a finding.
